In detail

The medieval centre — the Dom tower, the wharf cellars along the Oudegracht, and where every visitor to Utrecht stays. Utrecht publishes police registrations and survey results by wijk through its own research office. Registered crime across the city rose 10% in 2025, driven by home burglary, thefts from cars, bicycle theft and violence, and 59% of residents reported seeing at least one suspicious situation in their neighbourhood that year. The centre is not among the wijken the city's own 2025 figures single out for youth nuisance; those are Overvecht, Zuidwest and Noordwest, all residential and all outside the ring. What a visitor meets here is bicycle theft, which is Utrecht's most ordinary crime and the one the city counts most of.

Frequently asked questions

Is Binnenstad safe?

Wandroz currently rates Binnenstad in Utrecht as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Utrecht during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Utrecht at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Utrecht publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Binnenstad safe at night?

At night, Binnenstad is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Utrecht. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Binnenstad a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Binnenstad's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Utrecht) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Binnenstad?

Not an official government crime feed — Binnenstad's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used).
